purpose: Read-only CPU sampling of accepted pipeline, not performance acceptance.
findings: The producer is dominated by AC entropy: dense512 72.9%, noise12-512 75.3%, dense2048 85.7% of producer samples.
Producer waiting falls from 9.6% at dense512 to 0.5% at dense2048. The reconstruction worker waits for ready entropy in over half of its queued-thread samples.
Compaction is the largest clearly named worker compute category: dense512 443 samples, pack 197, named IDCT 66 plus 191 BLAS samples with incomplete caller stacks.
Dense512 AC direct code 1485/1715 samples; bitwise symbol fallback with its callees 174, separate magnitude readBits 36, fillBuffer 20.
Noise12-512 AC direct code 1564/1740 samples; bitwise fallback 85, magnitude readBits 52, fillBuffer 39.

The inlined 13-bit lookup/refill source line dominates direct AC samples. Disassembly shows buffer loads, variable shift, array bounds check, entry/run guard and bit-count update, followed by an 8-bit fallback probe on misses.
The 64-coefficient clear uses 8 paired vector stores, with no separate memset call. Source-line sample coalescing prevents exact per-instruction clear/refill attribution.
limits: Samples are wall-clock stack observations, not hardware CPU-cycle counters, hit/miss instrumentation or benchmark timings.
Sleeping main/runloop and thread-pool samples are reported separately; percentages use individual producer/worker thread denominators.
Worker samples include partial unwinds in BLAS. Named inverseDCT caller samples alone undercount transform work.
Long-code fallback cost does not establish its frequency; no 13-bit prefix miss-rate is claimed.
Sampling and host activity perturb execution; figures guide hypotheses only. No production files changed.
